A News Article That Embeds Tweets

By Test Reporter · January 15, 2026 · 4 minute read

News articles routinely cite social posts. Here are several embed shapes a third-party page might ship.

Case 1 — bare blockquote (no widgets.js)

This is the canonical static fallback that any site can paste. It works without widgets.js, so the markup is fully present:

Just shipped v2.0 with full #typescript support and a brand-new plugin API. Check it out at example.com — feedback welcome!

— Jane Developer (@janedev) January 10, 2026

Some interstitial article text between embeds so the layout finder doesn't treat the embeds as the entire content.

Case 2 — hidden blockquote + rendered iframe (widgets.js ran)

When widgets.js loads, it hides the source blockquote and inserts a cross-origin iframe sibling. Our extractor must dedupe and produce ONE card.

A second tweet with no embedded link, just text content.

— Sam Tester (@samtester) January 12, 2026

More body text between embeds to keep the article from being purely a sequence of tweet cards.

Case 3 — iframe only (no source blockquote)

Some pages strip the source blockquote after widgets.js renders, leaving only the iframe. In this case we render a stub card pointing at x.com.

— end of fixture
